why_angle: The cited Product Bible, Dashlore and Redline pages give cabin resolutions and maker specs, but none gives a cabin-camera data rate (Dashlore says it reports no bitrate). This page puts named testers' cabin figures side by side, at 23.8 Mb/s on the VIOFO T330 3CH against about 9.9 Mb/s on the N4 Pro S. That shows the camera most often called best overall records the thinnest cabin channel, and the cabin is the reason a rideshare driver buys a 3-channel camera.

page.h1: Best dash cam for rideshare drivers: 3-channel cameras with an infrared cabin view
page.desc: Which 3-channel dash cam records rideshare passengers best? We compare cabin resolution, infrared light and measured cabin data rates, plus parking-kit prices read 2026-11-21.
page.answer: Short answer. The best dash cam for rideshare drivers is the VIOFO T330 3CH: with all 3 channels recording, its 2K infrared cabin camera writes 23.8 Mb/s, 2.4 times the 1080p cabin of the Vantrue N4 Pro S, which costs less and wins on its 4K front.

page.after:
What the differences mean

Dealectric does not test dash cams. The figures here come from the makers' US stores and from named DashCamTalk and Mighty Gadget testers, all read 2026-11-21. For a rideshare driver, three figures decide the pick. First is the cabin camera's resolution and data rate with every channel recording, because that footage is the evidence in a passenger dispute. Second is whether the cabin camera has infrared light for night rides. Third is the front camera in the same mode, which covers crash and plate evidence.

  • Cabin pixels: 2560 × 1440 = 3.69 million pixels and 1920 × 1080 = 2.07 million, and 3.69 ÷ 2.07 = 1.8. The 2K cabin cameras on the T330 3CH, A329S 3CH and N4S therefore have 1.8 times the pixels of the cabin cameras on the N4 Pro S and N5S.
  • Cabin data: 23.8 ÷ 9.9 = 2.4, so the T330's cabin channel stores 2.4 times as much picture per second as the N4 Pro S's. For the N4S, 14.8 ÷ 9.9 = 1.5 times. Data rate stands in for detail; it is not a sharpness test.
  • Card use on the N4 Pro S: EricSan's files total 417,790 KB a minute with all three cameras on. That is 417,790 × 60 = 25.1 GB an hour, so a 256 GB card holds at most 256 ÷ 25.1 = 10.2 hours, which is barely one 10-hour shift. A 512 GB card holds 20.4 hours and a 1 TB card 39.8 hours. Vantrue's FAQ lets locked event clips use up to 30% of the card, so the loop keeps less than these totals.
  • Parking-ready cost of the pick: $499.99 + $25.99 for the HK6-F kit = $525.98 at VIOFO on 2026-11-21. The three Vantrue cameras take the $29.99 Voltage Display kit, which Vantrue lists for the N4S, N4 Pro S and N5S.

Why the cabin camera's data rate decides a rideshare dash cam

A rideshare complaint, such as an argument, a damage claim or an accusation, happens in the cabin, often at night, and usually with no impact. Vantrue's FAQ says a clip is locked into the event folder only when the G-sensor feels a hit. Otherwise it goes to the normal folder, where loop recording overwrites it. That makes the cabin channel's detail and the card's hours the evidence you actually keep. Lock a disputed ride by hand: on the N4 Pro S, a short press of the power button locks the current video, and EricSan notes the button sits behind the side cover with the card slot.

Resolution alone does not separate these cameras. The data each one writes per second does:

VIOFO's '4K 60fps' headlines describe the 1- and 2-channel versions. VIOFO titles the A329S 3CH '4K 30FPS Front', and its A329SW 2CH page says the 2-channel front runs at double the frame rate of the 3CH variants. Once the cabin camera is added, the front records at 30 fps.

For the money, Vantrue's cameras win the segments they lead. The N4S ({after:vantrue-nexus-4s}) has the best cabin channel of the three Vantrue cameras. Mighty Gadget's James Smythe found its infrared mode gives 'a clear black and white image of the cabin, with faces easily identifiable'. In exchange, its front camera drops to 2592 × 1944 when all three cameras record. BlackboxMyCar listed the same N4S at $179.99 on 2026-11-21, below Vantrue's {price:vantrue-nexus-4s} that day. {buy:vantrue-nexus-4s}

The N4 Pro S ({after:vantrue-nexus-4-pro-s}) is the pick for drivers who put road evidence first. EricSan measured 31.9 Mb/s from its 4K front, and its cabin has 4 IR LEDs at 1080p. It takes microSD cards up to 1 TB, the size a full-time shift needs. {buy:vantrue-nexus-4-pro-s}

The N5S ({after:vantrue-nexus-5s}) is the only camera here with a second infrared cabin camera aimed at the back row, which suits minivans and 3-row SUVs. Each of its two cabin cameras records 1080p at 9.8 Mb/s. {buy:vantrue-nexus-5s}
